title: Signal orchestration & evidence capture runbook
content:
Purpose:
This runbook documents the operational flow we use to: 1) orchestrate inbound security signals (alerts, telemetry, anomalous audit events), 2) capture and preserve forensic evidence automatically where possible, and 3) escalate to the right on-call and engineering owners with clear artifacts for containment and postmortem.

Scope and assumptions:
- Applies to production-hosted services, Dedicated endpoints, and any control-plane actions surfaced in audit logs.
- Assumes SIEM (Splunk/Elastic) receives forwarded audit logs and can host short-term evidence artifacts (snippets, search snapshots).
- Not a full forensic playbook for customer-owned on-prem systems — we provide capture primitives and evidence handoff guidance.
- RBAC v2 considerations: many automated captures depend on service account privileges; make sure these are defined in the RBAC policy catalog.

High-level signal flow (text diagram):
1) Detection: telemetry -> alert engine (anomaly/detection rules) -> alert ticket created in SEC queue.
2) Enrichment: automated enrichment job pulls related audit events, recent deploys, Kubernetes/instance snapshot metadata, and user session context.
3) Evidence orchestration: enrichment triggers evidence-capture tasks (log export, KV cache snapshot, memory-safe artifacts, package of matching audit events).
4) Routing & Escalation: runbook determines on-call routing (pager -> bridge owner -> platform/infra) and attaches evidence package.
5) Contain & Mitigate: owners perform containment actions. Evidence store is frozen for postmortem.
6) Postmortem & Lessons: fill short postmortem template and attach to ticket.

Roles & responsibilities (quick):
- First Responder (Pager): Does initial triage, confirms signal legitimacy, runs quick containment if trivial, requests help if needed.
- Bridge Owner (on-call lead): Opens bridge, coordinates enrichment and evidence collection, assigns engineers.
- Infra/Platform Eng: Runs containment steps that require infra privileges (e.g., revoke cloud API keys, scale down nodes).
- Applied ML / Model Ops: If model weights or prompts are implicated, owns model-level containment and snapshotting.
- SEC Forensics: Handles evidence preservation, chain-of-custody tagging, and SIEM snapshots for legal/audit.

Triage checklist (fast):
- Verify alert: Reproduce the indicator (search the alert query over the last 24h).
- Source identification: Which service, region, account, service account, or user triggered this?
- Scope estimate: Count unique principals, affected endpoints, and request IDs.
- Immediate risk: Is data exfiltration or privilege escalation suspected? If yes -> escalate immediately.
- Containment Start: If impact > medium, ask Bridge Owner to open bridge and call Infra.

Automated evidence-capture actions (what we run automatically on alerts with "capture=true"):
- Audit log slice export: time window = alert_time - 30m : alert_time + 30m; fields = timestamp, principal_type, principal_id, action, resource, request_id, trace_id, ip, user_agent, api_args (redact PII).
- SIEM search snapshot: create saved search & export artifacts (ndjson).
- Kubernetes context: kubectl get pods -o wide (labels/annotations), kubectl describe pod for matching request IDs, snapshot of pod env vars (only non-sensitive).
- Container logs tail: last 10k lines for relevant containers.
- Instance metadata: instance id, AMI/container image hash, running processes list (ps-like), open network connections (netstat-like) if permitted.
- KV cache prefix snapshot: for model-serving anomalies we snapshot affected cache prefixes and TTLs.
- Model request history: last 1k requests for endpoint, includes prompt hash and metadata (not full prompt if customer data flagged).
- Policy and deploy fingerprint: git commit hash, deploy job id.

Evidence packaging rules:
- Each package must include: capture_manifest.json (list of captures + timestamps), exported_log.ndjson, siem_snapshot_id, and the capture trigger context (alert id, rule id, bridge id).
- Minimal PII: always run sanitizers for customer content unless evidence retention authorized by a Tier2 manager.
- Retention class: evidence packages are tagged with EXPIRES=YYYY-MM-DD based on incident severity and legal hold requests.
- Chain-of-custody header: who requested the capture, who executed, and hashes of artifacts (sha256).

RBAC quick checklist before evidence capture (common failures):
- Confirm service account used for automated capture has least-privilege roles to read logs and list resources but not modify production state.
- If memory/disk snapshot requires elevated privileges, require temporary privilege elevation with approval (audit log must show elevation).
- Validate that KMS/HSM keys used for storing evidence are auditable and rotated per policy.

SIEM export mapping (audit_log schema -> SIEM fields):
- audit.timestamp -> @timestamp (ISO8601)
- audit.principal_type -> user.type (service|human|machine)
- audit.principal_id -> user.id
- audit.action -> event.action
- audit.resource.type -> resource.type
- audit.resource.id -> resource.id
- audit.request_id -> event.id
- audit.trace_id -> trace.id
- audit.ip -> client.ip
- audit.user_agent -> client.user_agent
- audit.outcome -> event.outcome (success|failure|denied)
- audit.extra -> event.metadata.* (flattened)

Sample SIEM query (pseudo-SPL/ES):
- Splunk-like: search index=audit_logs action=delete OR action=token.create OR action=deploy failure OR outcome=denied | stats count by user.id, action | where count>5
- Elastic-like: POST _search {"query": {"bool": {"must": [{"terms": {"event.action": ["token.create","deploy"]}}, {"range": {"@timestamp": {"gte": "now-1h"}}}]}}}

Escalation matrix (condensed):
- Low (no data exposure, single API error): Pager -> Bridge Owner if remains >1 hour -> close with note.
- Medium (suspicious activity, possible credential misuse): Pager -> Bridge Owner -> Infra (within 30m) -> evidence capture triggered.
- High (confirmed exfiltration, large privilege escalation, prod-wide impact): Pager -> Bridge Owner -> Pager + Exec-on-call notified -> Legal + Forensics auto-notified -> Incident declared and SEV-level bridge opened.

Containment play examples (prescriptive):
- Revoke short-lived tokens: call token service revoke API with request_id whitelist.
- Kill affected pods: kubectl delete pod <pod> --grace-period=0; capture logs before delete.
- Isolate network: apply deny rule for suspect IP at load balancer or security group.
- Rollback deployment: if new deploy correlates with anomaly, rollback to previous stable commit (document commit hash).

Evidence preservation commands (examples/responsibilities):
- Capture audit slice (SRE script): ./tools/export_audit_slice --rule ALERT-424 --from t0 --to t1 --out /tmp/evidence/alert-424-audit.ndjson
- Snapshot pod logs: ./tools/pod_log_capture --selector "app=model-serving,request_id=abc123" --lines 10000 --out /tmp/evidence/pod-abc123.log
- Create SIEM snapshot (Concourse job): POST /siem/api/snapshot {"query_id":"q-789","ttl":"7d"} -> returns snapshot_id.
- Hash artifacts: sha256sum <file> >> capture_manifest.json

Post-incident quick postmortem template (to fill in ticket):
- Title: short clear summary (one line)
- Incident ID: SEC-YYYY-NNN
- Timeline (UTC): bullets with timestamps and short actions (detection, containment, eradication, recovery)
- Root cause (short): one paragraph
- Blast radius & impact: what customers, services, or data were affected
- Containment actions taken: list + hashes of evidence packages
- Remediation plan & owners: 90-day action items with owners
- Follow-up checks (KPI): updated alerting threshold, SIEM rule tuning, RBAC policy updates
- Severity & classification: confidentiality/integrity/availability flags

Notes-to-self / running TODOs (working doc style):
- TODO: get SRE approval to add kubectl read-only role to capture service account (PR #789).
- TODO: add an automated "sanitizer" step to the capture pipeline to redact potential PII from model prompts before persisting.
- Question: do we keep full model prompts for internal infra investigations? Need legal input (ticket SEC-321).

Open issues and known gaps:
- Some legacy services log in a non-standard schema; enrichment jobs fail to map fields -> false negatives in correlation.
- Live forensic snapshots currently require manual approval for hosts in Dedicated clusters; goal: reduce friction while maintaining audit trail.
- SIEM cost for long-term storage of search snapshots is not solved; propose sliding retention tiers.

Appendix: quick references & links
- RBAC v2 policy catalog (living): confluence link in linked_artifacts.
- Evidence retention policy summary: EXPIRES=7d for low severity, 90d for medium, hold until legal for high.
- Contact list: Pager rota in ops/rota (see infra-ops-schedule), SEC oncall pager channel #sec-oncall.

This document is intentionally pragmatic and operational — treat it as a living checklist and add step-by-step capture scripts here as we stabilize them.

Signed: Aisha (sec-runbooks)
